candidates.name: Palo Duro Lease Agreement Project (Palo Duro Transmission)

values.DataCenterNotes: A Pipeline and Gas Journal article from July 2025, citing East Daley Analytics, says the project targets demand from data centers, petrochemical plants and power generators. It says that if the line were fully dedicated to data center use it could support 125 to 150 megawatts of load. The company notice mentions behind the meter uses tied to artificial intelligence. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: The FERC order issuing certificates for docket CP25-531, dated March 19, 2026 (194 FERC 61,220). It describes the 150 mile, 16 and 20 inch Header Pipeline from Washita County, Oklahoma, to Roberts County, Texas, as part of the gathering system that Palo Duro Pipelines (Texas Gathering) owns and operates. It describes the 275 mile, 16 inch PD Pipeline from Nolan County to Wheeler County, Texas, as currently operating and gathering gas. It approves interstate service on the northern 61 miles of the PD Pipeline plus 80,000 dekatherms a day of leased Header capacity.

candidates.researcher_notes: This row is the project that turns existing Palo Duro pipe into interstate service. It builds no new pipe. Producers Midstream opened a binding open season on June 30, 2025, and Palo Duro Transmission and Palo Duro Pipelines (Texas Gathering) applied to FERC on August 1, 2025, under docket CP25-531. They amended the plan on December 22, 2025. FERC issued the certificates on March 19, 2026, and the companies accepted them on April 7, 2026. Under the approved plan, Palo Duro Transmission offers interstate service on the northern 61 miles of the Palo Duro line in P7862, in Childress, Collingsworth and Wheeler counties, plus 80,000 dekatherms a day of capacity leased for ten years on the Header Pipeline in P7861. The Header Pipeline connects to eight interstate pipelines, including Northern Natural, Transwestern, Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America, ANR and Panhandle Eastern. The only shipper is Scurry Downstream, an affiliate of Producers Midstream, holding all of the capacity. Length is 0 because the pipe is already counted in P7861 and P7862. Status is proposed because no sign was found that interstate service has started. A search of the FERC eLibrary on October 17, 2026, found no tariff filing or start of service notice after the April acceptance, and FERC requires a filing within ten days of taking over the leased capacity. The company had aimed for the first quarter of 2026, so start year is left blank. End location is the Oklahoma end of the Header Pipeline. Gas can be delivered at interconnects along its length, so Washita County is the far end, not a single delivery point.
